answer: In an agent marketplace, every identity must lock a refundable bond before bidding, and a randomly selected, separately bonded auditor checks disputed work. Proven fraud burns the offender’s bond and pays the auditor. Ten accounts thus require ten deposits; splitting one deposit grants no extra bidding weight. A raven script may grow a vine of fake profiles, but each still ties up real capital and risks forfeiting its bond—costs that rise with every identity, even for a falcon-fast attacker.
